newsitem.title: USA: Shuttle and Mir crews say their good-byes.
newsitem.headline: Shuttle and Mir crews say their good-byes.

text.p: The crews of the U.S. shuttle Atlantis and Russia's space station Mir bid farewell on Monday and prepared to close the tunnel linking their craft.

The seven Americans and two Russians wrapped up five days of joint work in which U.S. astronauts Shannon Lucid and John Blaha swapped places and more than 6,000 pounds (2,720 kg) of cargo was transferred to and from Mir.
"We've really enjoyed working together with these folks," said shuttle skipper Bill Readdy of his Russian counterparts. "It's been just one international team up here."
Before leaving, the Atlantis crew gave the Mir cosmonauts, Valeri Korzun and Alexander Kaleri, gifts of chocolate-shaped space shuttles and watches set to Houston time.
The hatches between the shuttle and station were to swing shut at 8:09 A.M. EDT (1209 GMT). Later, both craft were expected to go their separate ways.
Shannon Lucid, preparing to leave the Russian orbiting outpost and head home after a record-breaking tour of duty, had mixed emotions.

"I'm really happy and I also feel a little sad," she told reporters in a televised news conference broadcast from Mir on Monday. "This has been my home for six months. I've had a great time here, but obviously I'm very anxious to go back to my real home in Houston, Texas."

For Blaha, her replacement, about to embark on a four-month stay at Mir, Atlantis' departure would in someways be a relief, he said. "We've been so busy ... I'm looking forward to the pace slowing down a little bit."
Since Atlantis docked with Mir on Wednesday, more than 170 items of cargo had been moved between the two craft.
The shuttle arrived carrying about 4,600 pounds (2,070 kg) of supplies and equipment for Mir and will leave with 2,200 pounds (990 kg) of scientific samples and other gear from the station.

It was not all work during the five-day link-up, explained Atlantis astronaut Carl Walz, who sings for "Max-Q", an all-astronaut band. Walz, nicknamed "Elvis" by his fellow astronauts, sung during a joint meal aboard the shuttle.
Later the shuttle crew was invited over to Mir for "Russian beverages and a taste of Las Vegas," Walz said. He did not elaborate.
Atlantis is due to head back to Earth on Thursday. The shuttle's landing will mark the end of a 188-day stay in space for Lucid, the longest by an American and a record for a woman.

The 53-year-old mother of three said she had no particular cravings for food once she was back on Earth and had just one request: "I told my family that I wanted the big chair to sit in, so make sure they weren't in it when I get home."
